description: aweb.usage/1 report batches (docs/app-usage.md §1-§5): valid batches with their canonical bytes and report_sha256 (bare hex SHA-256 of aweb.usage-report/1\n followed by the batch's canonical JSON); refused batches (schema_invalid); one installation's ordered collector steps with the expected ack, and the totals after them; and the lifecycle grant of a retired installation, each case marked `checked_by`: `batch` (decidable from the batch alone) or `collector` (needs the installation's state).

refusals.name: lone-surrogate
refusals.note: valid JSON whose team_id escapes a lone surrogate; it has no UTF-8 canonical form

collector.note: a known report_id with other bytes
accepted past a gap, which stays visible
overlaps stored sequences 2 and 3 with byte-identical entries; nothing is counted twice
an overlap that differs; nothing is stored
a snapshot past a gap becomes the reporter's current inventory
an older snapshot of the same epoch arriving later does not replace it; its entry fills the gap
another report repeating sequence 7 and its identical snapshot: stored once, nothing changes
the same snapshot identity (reporter, epoch 1, at_seq 7) with other gauges; the whole batch is refused
a new epoch's first snapshot replaces the old epoch's, although its sequence is lower
a delayed epoch-1 snapshot is stored but never replaces the current epoch's inventory

totals_after_collector.note: epoch 1 sequences 1-8 and epoch 2 sequence 1, each counted once; the reporter's inventory is epoch 2's

lifecycle_grant.name: new-installation-refuses-old-generation
lifecycle_grant.note: a report naming the new installation with the old generation
